_about: Source of truth for this file's names, enums and rooms. See chapters/ch2/chapter.json for the full note. Scene order is the enum order: the index in this list is the value Rive stores.

scene.about: Which room the stage shows. Setting the same value again does nothing.

direction.about: forward for Next, back for Back. Set before scene.

startScene.about: The scene the file opens on, already built and looping (no intro, pan or fade). Read once, on the file's first frame: set it and scene to the same value in onLoad. Same values as scene; the default is the file's usual opening scene.

scenes.name: loading
scenes.about: The file's default and the Start room before its bird arrives: the empty cream-and-orange room with the standard ball bouncing in the centre. It has no room of its own; the Start room draws it. Not a card; when scene becomes start the ball finishes its bounce, then the bird drops in (no pan, no colour change).

scenes.name: ad
scenes.about: The empty Chapter 1 room: no props, no ball. Ad 1 and Ad 2 play here, and it is the picture File 2 opens on (File 2's from-chapter-1).

tuneLater: **Card 1: the ball's story is this scene's loop** (762 frames, 12.7 s), and the only scene that follows the scene loop guideline so far. It starts the moment the intro ends: the ball slides out of the cuckoo clock's door along the blue perch, bounces on the chair and onto the window, the nine panes flip to tiles and back (the ball is knocked off), and it rolls off the right edge. Once it is out of sight it is removed (put back behind the clock door, also out of sight); 3 s later it slides out again, and the loop repeats. The ball never goes beyond x 1519, so it always leaves with its room. The small loops (their own "Chapter 1 Card 1 Small" layer, which starts when the pan ends) fit the loop with no jump: the minute hand turns twice (24 ticks), the pendulum swings 12 times, the dog's tail wags 3 times, the mouse runs once and waits in its hole, one set of clouds drifts across the whole window (hidden while the panes are tiles), the plant sways and drifts, and the dog's eye follows the mouse (it closes as the mouse approaches, stays closed while the mouse passes, opens once the mouse is past on its way home, and blinks while open). To tune: the shift per contact (the clock, shelf, chair, window, dog bed and floor each have their own), the pause (3.03 s), the eye's timing against the mouse, the dog's tail speed and the clouds' speed.

**Card 1: the ball's turning** (audited against the new global rule, 2026-11-02). The ball already rolled correctly (Ball Art rotation: one turn per circumference, clockwise rolling right, anticlockwise rolling left, constant spin in the air). The only change: on the window (loop 1.8 to 2.4 s) and on the dog bed (4.5 to 5.0 s) the ball rests but its rotation wobbled by up to 0.17 radians; those two windows are now held still (a ball at rest stops turning). Nothing else about the story or its timing changed.
**Card 1: the dog's eye.** It is asleep while the mouse is in front of it. If it still doesn't read as asleep, the next step is a bigger cue (the head dipping, or a small z).

**Card 2: the pencil knocks the stack, slide down, climb back up** (finesse round 5, physics, 2026-11-02; loop 499 frames, 8.3 s; the times are Finesse-panel timecodes of the first pass, and each later loop repeats them 8.3 s apart). Intro: the ball sits on the pink and orange block and rides it down (squash when it lands, 1.63 s); the pencil topples from upright into its leaning place (1.62 to 1.8 s) and lands against the stack at 1.8 s: the purple bar and the domino shiver. The teeter starts 3 frames later and takes a second (finesse round 6): three slow swings of a pendulum, eased through the middle and still only at the ends, a small rock right (1.85 to 2.17 s), a bigger rock back left (2.17 to 2.5 s), then a third swing right that goes past the balance point (2.5 to 2.98 s). The ball rolls with the tilt, never stops, and accelerates through the tip (0.1 px per frame at 2.5 s to 1.8 at the end) and off the block's right end at 2.95 s while the block is still tipping (to 23 degrees at 2.98 s); then the block rocks back and settles (about 0.6 s). From here the path is simulated with one gravity (0.40) and every contact keeping 70 to 90 percent of its speed: it lands on the purple bar at 3.18 s (71% kept; the bar dips, the domino wobbles), bounces into the pencil at 3.35 s (88%; the pencil gives a little), falls past the right white joint onto the yellow stick at 3.73 s (70%; the stick flexes), rolls down it speeding up to 8 px per frame and leaves its low end at 3.83 s (the lower-left joint squashes), lands on the floor line at 4.0 s moving left (46% kept: the floor takes the fall; its spin carries on), rolls a short way, slows and stops at 4.2 s (x 577, its left edge at the 560 line; the spin stops too), pauses 0.27 s, and at 4.47 s rolls back right along the floor line, speeding up for 0.6 s to 3.6 px per frame, passing behind TOTAL (hidden for about 0.4 s by a hole cut in the ball's clip, which is switched on only for this run), behind the C block at 5.48 s (the block gets a nudge) and stopping at the pencil's foot at 6.12 s (0.3 s pause). The climb, six small steps: onto the C block's top (6.97 s, the block dips), the green slab's right end (7.6 s, the slab dips), three steps up the purple bar (8.15, 8.57 and 8.98 s) and back onto the block with a small hop (9.48 s; the block tips a little under it), then it rolls to its spot as the block settles and the teeter starts again. The ball turns as it rolls. Adapted to the art: the stack is tall, so at one gravity the ball falls fast (up to 10.5 px per frame at the stick and the floor) and the whole slide from the bar to the floor takes 0.8 s, where the earlier version took 1.6 s; the TOTAL slide is gone, because the yellow stick ends at the lower-left joint, to the left of TOTAL's edge, so nothing physical carries the ball onto TOTAL's left edge (a ball that leaves the stick moving left at 8 px per frame lands on the floor beyond it): TOTAL is now only passed behind on the way back; the ball just misses the right white joint (2 px) so the joint squashes only for the climb; the pencil can't physically reach the block (its eraser end stops 100 px to its right), so the topple lands against the bar and the shiver runs down to the block. The ball's highest point is y 402 (395 px on the 375 x 812 phone frame, 144 px below the lowest copy line). To tune: every time above, the teeter (the three swings: size and length of each), the floor run (how far left, the pause, how fast it comes back), the hop heights, how hard each piece reacts.

**Card 3: the #1 mug circuit** (finesse rounds 5 and 6, physics, 2026-11-03; loop 219 frames, 3.65 s; the times are Finesse-panel timecodes of the first pass, and each later loop repeats them 3.65 s apart). The ball starts hidden inside the mug (a clip hides it below the mug's front rim) and the journey starts inside the intro as soon as the pan has landed: the mug rocks at 1.67 s and the ball hops out at 1.8 s in one plain parabola up over the left white post, peaks 80 px above the band (y 377) and drops almost straight onto the yellow band at 2.78 s. The band sags quickly (the ball 8 px, the band's middle 20 px, over 6 frames, 0.1 s) and throws it back up and left at 96% of the speed it arrived with (2.88 s). It flies left to the leaning books and ricochets off their right face at 3.18 s (88% kept): the books are knocked back 6 degrees about their base in 4 frames, rock once forward (3 degrees) and once back and settle in 0.4 s (3.18 to 3.6 s). It flies right to the FIRST card and ricochets off its left edge at 3.48 s (84%; the card wobbles), flies left and hits the white knob at the stick's top at 3.83 s (about 80%), which turns it back to the right; it lands on the blue stick at 3.88 s (87% kept). The stick visibly bends at the contact (4.6 degrees about its low end, a 9 px dip at the top end, in 3 frames), the ball rides it down, and the stick springs back with one small overshoot over 0.3 s (3.88 to 4.2 s). The ball rolls the last bit speeding up (10 px per frame) and at 4.0 s the stick's spring-back lifts it off the low end: it keeps 71% of its speed (7.9 px per frame) and leaves almost straight up (82 degrees above horizontal, a little to the right), peaks at y 585, clears the mug's left rim by about 50 px, comes down nearly straight (8 degrees off vertical) through the mug's mouth at x 733 and passes below the rim line at 4.73 s, out of sight at 4.77 s; the mug wobbles (4 frames in, 2 small rocks, 0.4 s) and waits out of sight about 0.5 s before the mug rocks and the ball hops out again (second pass 5.45 s). The ball turns as it rolls, keeps its spin in the air (the lift keeps the fast spin it had rolling at 10 px per frame) and gets a little spin on each ricochet; the turn that is left over at the end of the loop is taken up while the ball is hidden in the mug. The shelf and the posts do not move. Adapted: the hop out of the mug has to rise 345 px to above the band, so at one gravity it takes 1.0 s (59 frames); the band can only return about the speed it received, and the books are 150 px away, so the throw off the band is a low arc to the left (20 degrees above horizontal); the ball cannot arrive at the stick's top moving left and roll up to the knob (it would bounce off the stick), so it flies from the FIRST card's ricochet straight into the knob, which throws it down onto the stick near its low end; the roll down the stick is short (0.1 s); the lift off the stick's end is a spring-back, so the ball arrives at 10.9 px per frame and leaves at 7.9, and the lob takes 0.73 s (44 frames) from the stick end to the rim. The ball's highest point is y 377 (371 px on the 375 x 812 phone frame, 120 px below the lowest copy line). To tune: every time above, the wait in the mug, how hard the books, the stick and the mug react.

**Card 4: balance, streak, down to the pot and back up** (finesse rounds 4 and 6, 2026-11-03; loop 612 frames, 10.2 s; the times are Finesse-panel timecodes of the first pass, and each later loop repeats them 10.2 s apart). The pot and flowers ride in with the pan, and so does the ball: it is already rocking on the crossword head as the room slides into view (finesse round 6). Lead-in (0 to 1.6 s, the first visit only): it rolls 3 px right (0.1 to 0.5 s), 6 px back left (0.67 to 1.07 s) and 3 px home (1.23 to 1.6 s), slowly and calmly, with the head tilting under it like a scale (1.3 degrees); the loop never plays it again. Balance (1.6 to 3.2 s, and at the start of every later loop): it is never still: short rolls of about 8 px on the head's flat top separated by pauses of 0.13 to 0.4 s, and the head tilts under it like a scale. The streak (3.27 to 5.13 s): even hops (0.57 s in the air, 0.08 s on the flower) from the crossword head to the yellow S hexagon (lands 3.83 s), to the purple leaf (4.48 s) and home to the head (5.13 s); each flower dips and tilts under the landing and springs back. A short balance (5.13 to 6.3 s). Down to the pot (6.3 to 7.9 s): it rolls to the head's right edge (the head tips) and off it at 6.67 s, falls onto the hexagon's slope at 6.9 s and slides down it, drops onto the blue leaf at 7.65 s (it bends and springs back; the landing now eases from 4 px per frame to 2 over four frames, no stall), slides down its edge and drops onto the pot's rim at 7.82 s. The rim (7.82 to 9.35 s; the last roll back is 14 frames instead of 8): it rolls along it with pauses of 0.13 to 0.17 s. The climb (9.45 to 11.12 s): three small hops, touching the blue leaf at 9.95 s (it bends), landing on the hexagon at 10.53 s and on the crossword head at 11.12 s, then it settles and balances again (the balance of the next pass starts at 11.78 s). The ball turns as it rolls (clockwise rolling right, anticlockwise rolling left) and keeps its spin in the air. Adapted to the art: the flowers are in front of the ball, so the ball falls behind them on the way down and up (hidden for about 0.2 s behind the head's corner and the purple leaf's tip); the way from the head to the blue leaf goes by the hexagon's slope because the head is directly above the leaf; the blue leaf is too steep to rest on, so the ball touches it for 3 frames on the climb. The hops are low: 38, 62 (it has to clear the crossword head), 24 high; the climb steps are 22, 26 and 22 high. The loop picks up at 3.2 s inside the balance's last pause and closes on that pose. **The speed check still flags these, on purpose; they are part of why this room feels right (Demetre, 2026-11-03):** the softer gravity (flights fall at 0.17 to 0.31 per frame squared instead of 0.40: the streak hops, the slides off the hexagon and the leaf, the climb hops), the contact at 3.95 s that leaves faster than it arrived (5.4 to 7.2, the landing on the hexagon, also listed as a turn-round) and the contact at 10.57 s that leaves faster than it arrived (2.4 to 4.2, the push-off from the hexagon). Jitter fixed in round 6: the buzz after the last landing (the flower, head and ball now dip once, no rocking), the 2-frame stop in the blue leaf's spring-back, and the lurches and stalls on the blue leaf's landing and the rim's last roll. The ball's highest point is y 446 (439 px on the 375 x 812 phone frame, 188 px below the lowest copy line). To tune: every time above, the length of the lead-in, the two balances and the rim, how far each flower dips, the tilt of the head.

**Card 5: Wordle Bot and the ball's climb** (finesse round 2, 2026-11-03, `chapters/ch1/ch1_card_5.py`; loop 406 frames, 6.75 s; Finesse-panel timecodes of the first pass, each later loop repeats them 6.75 s apart). The six WORDLE blocks are at 70 percent (their lines stay 1.5), the L block's left face at x 618, the right end at x 866.5; the O and W blocks drop with their shadows (1.0 to 1.5 s, squash to 1.82 s); the second bottom block's letter is the R of WORDLE (it was a B). Wordle Bot, at Figma's size (scale 5.3461, body 117.8 wide), stands on the floor behind the blocks' right end: his body shows above the right step, the blocks stay in front of him so every letter shows, and his tapping right shoe stands clear of the E. He is copied in from his Rive file (2702548), not nested, so his keys are on the room's own timelines. His Drop In - Foot Tap starts at 1.35 s, while the blocks are still falling (starting it when they settle, 1.82 s, would land him at 2.37 s, after the copy), and lands at 1.9 s. His lines are 1.5, the room's weight (his strokes were 0.954 in his own units; Figma's bot is 2); the antennae, legs, shoes and laces, drawn as filled outlines, are redrawn as 1.5 strokes on the same centrelines; the soles are white, as in Figma. His head: the dome's centre x 868.4, its top y 545.5, the antenna tips up to y 533.4 (for the speech bubble's tail). The ball (radius 17, as in cards 2 to 4) rides in with the room at its home on the floor left of the blocks (x 585.5). At 2.02 s it hops onto the L block (2.57 s), pauses, and at 3.43 s hops onto the top row (the L block tips back a little as it pushes off) and perches there (3.9 s): the bot's screen tiles flash green twice and his foot tap follows like a nod (4.15 to 4.48 s). At 4.73 s it rolls right, off the top row at 5.98 s, falls behind the bot's body onto the right step (6.3 s, keeps 72 percent) and bounces; out of sight it is put back behind the bottom row (6.47 s) and rolls out from behind the L block to its home (7.12 to 7.95 s). His Idle (antenna twitch, screen tiles, foot tap) plays twice a loop (5.33 and 7.37 s), its taps falling while the ball is out of sight and at home. Every hop falls at 0.40; the hops' tops are y 580.6 and 521.7 (the bubble's lowest edge is y 502.7). The whole group and the ball's path are inside the phone frame (x 567.8 to 926.2). To tune: every time above, the pauses, the hops' heights, the flash, how far the L block tips.

**Card 1: pieces outside the safe area** (x 560 to 935, y 0 to 812; found in the global pass, nothing moved, a room-by-room call): the Mouse and its Mouse Hole Clip (x 958 to 984, y 697 to 711), the Mouse Hole (x 1069 to 1090, y 692 to 712) and the Outlet (x 930 to 944, y 681 to 703), all past the right line. They are the pieces the ball passes as it rolls off the right edge, which is part of its story.
